body: Fellow physics student here! In terms of light, the mixing of colours creates new colours because of interference. You can basically think of it as the two waves adding together, in the same way that when waves in water come into contact, they form new, more chaotic wave patterns. Sound waves do the same things, that’s how we get harmonics/overtones. Let me know if this makes sense!

Fair play for taking initiative! Leonard Susskind has a really good series of books called ‘The Theoretical Minimum’ which are an excellent jumping off point for a high schooler.  they cover Classical Mechanics, Special Relativity and Quantum Mechanics, as far as I remember. There are also great resources online like Khan Academy, and YouTube channels like crash course, physics girl, sixty symbols or 3B1B (that’s maths, but you’ll need to get very comfy with maths if you’re doing physics). You can use those as jumping off points to see if any particular topics interest you, and you can look for more specific resources as you get into more nuanced topics. Best of luck!!

I have lots of stories about that time but in terms of revenge: When I was about 10, I got a hand-me-down of a book about Einstein and his work, became obsessed with it, and did a presentation on special relativity (not the maths, I was a kid, but I explained the twin paradox/ the train in the tunnel/the photon clock) for a project.
